subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should a Claw manifest be allowed to install a process-wide plugin, and if so what explicit host-level authorization must the consented plan require?
rationale: The implementation can bind package identity and integrity to consent, but only maintainers can define whether that consent is sufficient for a plugin that changes the shared runtime for sibling agents.

options.title: Require shared-host authorization
options.body: Keep plugin packages only when the plan and apply flow include an explicit higher-scope grant that makes the process-wide effect visible to the operator.

options.title: Defer plugin mutation
options.body: Restrict this lifecycle to workspace-scoped skills until the Claw product model defines safe shared-plugin ownership and removal semantics.

options.title: Accept manifest-level consent
options.body: Treat package consent in a Claw declaration as sufficient authorization for shared plugin installation and document the cross-agent effect.

recommendation.title: Require shared-host authorization
recommendation.body: Keep plugin packages only when the plan and apply flow include an explicit higher-scope grant that makes the process-wide effect visible to the operator.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identifies the precise role-boundary decision that remains unresolved.
